reason: The text consistently portrays Yahweh as actively supporting and benefiting the Hebrew people. Key passages demonstrate this: (1) Yahweh has given the land to the Israelites ('נתן יהוה לכם את־ הארץ'); (2) Yahweh caused fear to fall upon the inhabitants of Canaan ('נפלה אימתכם עלינו'), which supports Israelite military advantage; (3) Yahweh performed miracles on behalf of Israel, drying up the Red Sea for their exodus ('הוביש יהוה את־ מי ים־ סוף מפניכם'); (4) Yahweh enabled Israelite victories over the Amorite kings ('וכי שמענו את אשר הובישׁ יהוה'). Throughout the passage, Yahweh's actions are presented as gifts and protective interventions for the benefit of the Hebrew people, not antagonism toward them.
